newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST-CPI concerns pressure Portugal bond sale.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-CPI concerns pressure Portugal bond sale.

text.p: Concerns over January inflation data, due to be released on Friday, will pressure yields at the state's auction for 20 billion escudos each of three-, five- and 10-year fixed-rate bonds, analysts and traders said.
If it considers the yields too high, the Institute for Public Credit Management (IGCP) may opt not to place all the paper on offer, they said. Results of the auctions are due around 1100 GMT.
Analysts expected bids for the March 2000 bonds at between 5.45 and 5.55 percent, in line with the 5.50 percent at the last auction on Wednesday.

Bids for the March 2002 bonds were expected between 5.75 and 5.85 percent, against 5.72 percent at the last auction on January 27, while those for the February 2007 bonds were seen at 6.65-6.75 percent, down from 6.83 percent on February 4.

Bids for the 10-year paper were therefore likely to be significantly higher than the secondary market where the paper closed at 6.58 percent on Thursday. There has so far been little secondary market trade in the March 2000 and 2002 series.

Analysts expect Portuguese consumer price inflation to stand at between 0.3 and 0.8 percent month-on-month in January, pushing the year-on-year rate up to between 3.3 and 3.8 percent compared with 3.3 percent in December.
